questions.q: A trading services licensee arranges a lease for a landlord. Which may they also do?
choices: Sign the lease on the owner's behalf
questions.explain: Trading licensees can find tenants, negotiate the lease, get the tenant's signature and collect the security deposit. Collecting rent, signing for the owner and inspections are rental property management.
questions.ref: Lesson 5 · Property management by trading licensees

questions.q: How may a trading-only licensee be paid for leasing a property?
choices: A one-time fee for the leasing service
A percentage of each month's rent
Any arrangement the owner agrees to
questions.explain: A trading licensee may charge a one-time fee for the leasing. Ongoing monthly fees suggest unlicensed property management.
questions.ref: Lesson 5 · Property management by trading licensees

questions.q: A trading-only licensee's client asks them to keep managing the rental after the lease is signed. Best response?
choices: Refer the client to a property management licensee, or get licensed in rental property management first
questions.explain: Ongoing management needs a rental property management licence. Refer it out or take the supplemental course and get licensed.
questions.ref: Lesson 5 · Property management by trading licensees

questions.q: Under Rules ss.94–95, whose rentals may a licensee manage without a property management licence?
choices: Their own, and their spouse's, children's or parents'
Any client who signs a waiver
questions.explain: The exemption covers the licensee, spouse, children and parents only, with written disclosures and no pay.
questions.ref: Lesson 5 · Property management by trading licensees

questions.q: Which is NOT a condition of the family rental exemption in Rules ss.94–95?
choices: Tell tenants the services aren't regulated under RESA
Run it through your brokerage's trust account
questions.explain: The conditions are your own name, telling tenants it's not regulated, written disclosure to the family member and managing broker, and no pay. It's done outside the brokerage.
questions.ref: Lesson 5 · Property management by trading licensees

questions.q: When must a licensee deliver a deposit received from a buyer to the brokerage?
questions.explain: "Promptly" means immediately: not after acceptance, not after subject removal.

questions.q: Where must a brokerage's trust accounts be kept?
choices: Interest-bearing trust accounts at a BC savings institution
questions.explain: RESA s.26 requires interest-bearing trust accounts at one or more savings institutions in BC.

questions.q: A buyer's deposit cheque is made payable to the seller's lawyer. What should the licensee do?
choices: Deposit it to the brokerage trust account
It may simply be delivered to the payee
Cash it and hold the money
questions.explain: Cheques payable to a third party, not the brokerage, may just be delivered to that party.

questions.q: In what capacity does a brokerage hold a deposit paid under a purchase agreement?
choices: As a stakeholder, not as agent for either party
questions.explain: RESA s.28: the brokerage holds deposits as a stakeholder, so it can't release them just because its own client asks.

questions.q: A deal collapses and both parties claim the $50,000 deposit. When can the brokerage release it?
choices: When both parties agree in writing, a court orders it, or the money is paid into court
When the managing broker decides who's right
questions.explain: As stakeholder, the brokerage needs written agreement of both parties, a court order or payment into court (or another permitted ground).

questions.q: A buyer rescinds under the Home Buyer Rescission Period. How is the deposit handled?
choices: All of it goes to the seller
All of it goes back to the buyer
The rescission fee goes to the seller and the balance to the buyer
It's held until a court decides
questions.explain: The brokerage may pay the 0.25% rescission fee to the seller and return the rest to the buyer.

questions.q: Which is a permitted reason to withdraw money from trust?
choices: To cover the brokerage's rent temporarily
To pay remuneration the brokerage has earned, as permitted
To pay the brokerage's E&O premium
questions.explain: Withdrawals include mistakes, REFBC interest, earned remuneration, unclaimed money, payment into court, court orders and principal's instructions.

questions.q: Where does interest on a client-requested separate trust account go?
questions.explain: For a separate account the client asks for, the interest goes as the client chooses. General trust account interest goes to REFBC.

questions.q: A buyer wants to pay the deposit in Bitcoin. What's the issue?
choices: None, because crypto can be held in trust
Crypto can't be held in a brokerage trust account; a third party would hold it without RESA protection, so warn the buyer, recommend legal advice and document it
It must be converted by the licensee personally
Only commercial deals can use crypto
questions.explain: Crypto can't go in trust. Explain the risks (no RESA protection, volatility), recommend legal advice and keep records.

questions.q: A buyer pays a large deposit, then their offer quickly fails and they ask for a refund to a different person. What's the concern?
choices: Possible money laundering, using the trust account to make money look clean; tell your managing broker
Only the bank needs to worry
questions.explain: Deposit, failed deal, refund is a classic laundering pattern. Raise it with your managing broker.

questions.q: Which Rules section requires licensees to act honestly and with reasonable care and skill?
questions.explain: Rules s.33 is honesty and s.34 is reasonable care and skill. Both are among the most commonly cited in discipline.
questions.ref: Lesson 5 · A map of the Rules

questions.q: Which Part of the Rules deals with relationships with principals and parties: agreements, disclosures, remuneration and dual agency?
questions.explain: Part 5 is Relationships with Principals and Parties. Part 9 is exemptions; Part 3 is general responsibilities.
questions.ref: Lesson 5 · A map of the Rules

questions.q: Which is an example of professional misconduct under RESA s.35?
choices: Acting contrary to the public's best interests
Incompetence in performing real estate services
questions.explain: Incompetence is listed as professional misconduct. The other three describe conduct unbecoming a licensee.

questions.q: Who may file a complaint against a licensee?
questions.explain: Anyone may complain, and BCFSA can also investigate without a complaint.

questions.q: A licensee makes a minor, obvious mistake. BCFSA proposes a written promise to fix it and comply in future. What is this?
questions.explain: An undertaking (s.53.1) is a written promise used for minor matters. It isn't published, but breaching it is misconduct.

questions.q: During an investigation, what does Rules s.21 require of a licensee?
choices: Nothing until a hearing is ordered
Respond to BCFSA promptly, in writing, within the time required
questions.explain: Licensees must respond promptly, in writing and on time. Not cooperating is itself professional misconduct.

questions.q: What's the minimum notice for a discipline hearing?
questions.explain: Notice of a discipline hearing must be given at least 21 days before the hearing.

questions.q: Which is true about a consent order?
choices: It's based on the licensee's proposal, is published, and can support a Special Compensation Fund claim but not a civil claim
It can be used as an admission in a civil lawsuit
It requires a full hearing first
questions.explain: A consent order comes from the licensee's proposal, it's public, and it can be used for Compensation Fund claims but not in civil proceedings.

questions.q: When may BCFSA make an urgent order under s.45?
choices: Without notice or a hearing, when the public interest requires it, for example to suspend a licence
questions.explain: Urgent orders can be made without notice or a hearing. The licensee gets reasons and a right to demand a hearing.

questions.q: What's the maximum discipline penalty for a brokerage under s.43?
questions.explain: Up to $500,000 for a brokerage and $250,000 for anyone else, per contravention.

questions.q: What may BCFSA order besides a penalty, to strip the gain from misconduct?
choices: Return of compensation, up to the remuneration received
questions.explain: Section 43 allows an order to pay back remuneration received from the contravention, plus enforcement expenses.

questions.q: Where does discipline penalty money go?
questions.explain: Penalty money may only be used for education.

questions.q: Are discipline decisions made public?
choices: Yes; s.47 requires publication and decisions are linked in the BCFSA licensee search
questions.explain: Orders are published, linked in the licensee search and often on CanLII.

questions.q: A licensee disagrees with a discipline decision. Where and how fast must they appeal?
choices: Financial Services Tribunal, in writing within 30 days
questions.explain: Appeals go to the Financial Services Tribunal, in writing within 30 days.

questions.q: While an appeal to the Financial Services Tribunal is pending, what happens to the order?
choices: It stays in effect unless the tribunal orders otherwise
It's doubled if the appeal fails
questions.explain: Filing an appeal doesn't stay the order; it stays in effect.

questions.q: What's the maximum administrative penalty per contravention?
questions.explain: Administrative penalties go up to $100,000 per contravention, often with courses or conditions.

questions.q: Which administrative penalty category carries the highest amounts?
questions.explain: Category F, unlicensed activity, has the highest penalty ranges.

questions.q: After receiving notice of an administrative penalty, how long does a licensee have to pay or ask for a hearing?
questions.explain: They have 30 days to pay or request a hearing.

questions.q: What's the maximum penalty for an individual's first RESA offence (e.g. trading without a licence)?
choices: A fine up to $1.25 million and/or up to 2 years' imprisonment
questions.explain: Offences carry up to $1.25 million (first) or $2.5 million (subsequent) and/or up to 2 years in prison for individuals.

questions.q: What does REDMA regulate?
choices: Developers marketing development units in development property
questions.explain: REDMA regulates how developers market development units, including units elsewhere if they're marketed in BC.

questions.q: How many strata lots in a building make it "development property" under REDMA?
questions.explain: Five or more for strata lots, bare land strata lots, subdivision lots, time shares and leasehold units.

questions.q: For which units does REDMA apply at only 2 or more?
choices: Cooperative interests and shared interests in land
questions.explain: Co-op interests and shared interests in land are development property at 2 or more.

questions.q: A developer is marketing 20 strata units in a building zoned and used for industrial purposes. Does REDMA apply?
choices: No; industrial/commercial zoned and used developments are exempt
questions.explain: Industrial or commercial developments zoned and used for those purposes are exempt, which matters for commercial practice.

questions.q: Before a licensee acting for a developer has a buyer sign a purchase agreement for a new strata unit, what must happen?
choices: The disclosure statement must have been filed, given to the buyer, and the buyer's written acknowledgement obtained
The buyer must have a lawyer
questions.explain: No agreement until the buyer gets the filed disclosure statement, has a chance to read it and acknowledges receipt in writing.

questions.q: What may a developer do before filing a disclosure statement?
choices: Pre-market, as long as there's no impression of a right to buy and ads carry the required disclaimer
questions.explain: Pre-marketing is allowed if it doesn't suggest buyers can buy yet, and ads include the developer's name and address, a contact and a prominent disclaimer.

questions.q: How long does a buyer have to rescind a REDMA purchase for any reason?
choices: 7 days after the later of the agreement or the written acknowledgement
questions.explain: The 7-day right runs from the later of the agreement and the buyer's written acknowledgement of the disclosure statement.

questions.q: A buyer never received a disclosure statement. When can they rescind?
questions.explain: Without a disclosure statement the buyer can rescind at any time, and the agreement is generally unenforceable.

questions.q: Does the Home Buyer Rescission Period apply to a REDMA pre-sale?
choices: Yes, in addition to the 7-day right
No; REDMA sales have their own rescission rights
Only if the deposit is over 5%
questions.explain: The HBRP doesn't apply to sales covered by REDMA's rescission rights.

questions.q: A purchase agreement includes a clause where the buyer waives their REDMA rescission right. What's the effect?
choices: The waiver is valid if signed
The right can't be waived, and a licensee using such an agreement risks discipline
It's valid if the buyer has a lawyer
questions.explain: REDMA rescission rights can't be waived. Licensees have been disciplined over agreements trying to do this.

questions.q: When does a developer have to file a new disclosure statement, rather than an amendment?
choices: When the developer changes, a receiver/liquidator/trustee is appointed, or BCFSA requires it
questions.explain: A new statement is required in those three cases, and it gives buyers a new 7-day rescission right. Amendments don't.
